# Draft:King of New York (photoseries)

King of New York, also abbreviated to K.O.N.Y., is a series of photographs taken by Barron Claiborne of American rapper the Notorious B.I.G., also known as Biggie Smalls. It was captured on March 6, 1997, in New York City three days before Biggie was killed in Los Angeles, California, making it one of the last photographs of the rapper. Claiborne captured the photo of Biggie to be used as the cover of Rap Pages Magazine.
Claiborne had given Biggie a plastic crown prop, later stating "Every time I thought of Biggie, I always thought of him as a big, fat West African King". Despite rapper Puff Daddy's concerns that Biggie would resemble the Burger King, which Biggie assured to Puff Daddy would not happen, Biggie used the crown for a photoshoot, with it tilting on his head.
King of New York is one of the most iconic photographs of Biggie and a visual representation of his title as the "King of New York". The photograph has been used many times, with it even inspiring Biggie's posthumous album Duets: The Final Chapter (2005).
Background
Claiborne had been hired by Rap Pages Magazine to do a photoshoot of Biggie for their front cover. Claiborne made the decision to picture Biggie as a king. Claiborne said in an interview "Every time I thought of Biggie, I always thought of him as a big, fat West African King." According to Claiborne in an interview with Angie Martinez, he had bought a plastic crown at the store Gordon Novelty, a store on Broadway at around 21st and 22nd Sts. Rapper Puff Daddy, who booked the photo shoot for Biggie, was concerned that Biggie would look like the "burger king"
However, Puff Daddy said that Biggie would look like the "Burger King"
